summary: Tests pass and the template/CSS changes meaningfully improve current and available destination presentation without changing travel contracts. However, a required acceptance criterion is not satisfied: unavailable destinations are never rendered. The implementation report confirms they are not supplied by the existing view model, while the added unavailable-state CSS is only an unused hook. Satisfying this would require either widening scope to expose unavailable destinations or revising the approved criterion, triggering the stated stop condition.
risks: Players cannot see or distinguish unavailable destinations because no unavailable destination markup is rendered.
The unavailable-state styling is untested in actual rendered output and may conceal an unmet product requirement.
Exposing blocked routes may require backend/view-model changes that are forbidden by the approved task.
